title: Seeing Small Amounts at a Glance
short: Know 1 to 5 dots without counting them one by one.

blocks.html: You know how to count to find how many. For small groups, you can often just see how many, fast!

blocks.name: k-pic
blocks.cap: Dot patterns like on a die: 3 in a line, 4 in a square, 5 is a square with one in the middle.

blocks.html: Groups of 1 to 5 can be seen at a glance, without counting one by one.
Our eyes can take in about 3 or 4 things at once, without counting. Patterns help with a few more: once you know the shape of 5 on a die, you just see it.

blocks.title: A quick look
blocks.q: A die shows four dots in the corners and one dot in the middle. How many dots?
steps: One more in the middle makes 5.

blocks.name: tenframe
blocks.cap: Look quickly! How many counters did you see? Press “Look again” to check.

blocks.html: For grown-ups: Play quick-look games with dice, dominoes or fingers: show for a moment, hide, then ask how many. Keep it to 5 or fewer at first.

sources.name: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics, Kindergarten, K.CC.B.5: count to answer “how many?” questions about up to 20 things
